notes: Drive times are free-flow estimates without traffic.
An asterisk on rent means a special offer applies; see the rent terms.
A floor marked 'read from the unit number' is not stated on the page; confirm it on the tour.
A place with an asterisk has one thing still to confirm (elevator, floor, dog policy or a live re-check of the listing); the text beside it says what and why.
Unknown cost lines count as $0 and are named on each receipt.

years.label: The Quiet-Street Year
years.subhead: An apartment tucked among houses and lawns: the lowest crime on the list and almost nothing on foot.

years.label: The Little-City Year
years.subhead: Small cities and inner suburbs with a real downtown: a car for errands, a main street for Friday night.

years.label: The Fresh-Start Year
years.subhead: New towers beside the water, where one neighbor in five moved in this year and everyone is looking to meet people.

years.label: The Walk-Everywhere Year
years.subhead: Old city blocks built before cars, where dinner, coffee and friends are a walk away and the car mostly sits.

years.label: The Old-Neighborhood Year
years.subhead: Long-settled apartment districts where the avenue feeds everyone and the neighbors have been there for years.

years.label: The Room-to-Breathe Year
years.subhead: Older suburbs where the money buys the most space, families live next door and most things are a drive.

parking_rules.summary: When the mayor declares a snow emergency, wintertime alternate-side parking starts: park on the even-numbered side from 7 AM on even dates to 7 AM the next day, and on the odd-numbered side on odd dates. The city's all-night parking restrictions on designated streets are suspended meanwhile.

parking_rules.quote: The first vehicle in the household will be $15.00 for a one-year period; the second vehicle $25.00; the third vehicle $50.00; and the fourth vehicle and above will be $100.00 for each permit.

parking_rules.summary: A car with out-of-state plates can get an Out-of-State Plate Permit with proof of residency: $50 for three months.
parking_rules.quote: Parking permits are issued to individuals upon presentation of proof of residency to use on their out-of-state registered vehicles. Out-of-state permits can be purchased at a cost of $50.00 for a period of three (3) months.

parking_rules.summary: New residents get a free two-week Temporary Permit while they change the address on their licence and registration.
parking_rules.quote: we provide a two (2) week Temporary Permit free of charge so new residents have sufficient time to change the address on their driver's license and vehicle registration.

parking_rules.summary: Visitor permits are issued for one vehicle and allow parking near the residence, except during posted street cleaning or emergency restrictions.
parking_rules.quote: Vehicles displaying this permit may park near the residence for which the permit is issued, except during posted street cleaning periods or temporary/emergency restrictions.

parking_rules.summary: Residential permit holders do not pay for overnight parking in non-reserved municipal lots.
parking_rules.quote: Holders of valid residential permits need not pay for overnight parking at any non-reserve municipal parking lot.

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's licence check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
parking_rules.quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A licence costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

dog_rules.summary: Licence fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
dog_rules.quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

dog_rules.summary: With proof of a current licence and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
dog_rules.quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's licence check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
parking_rules.quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A licence costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

dog_rules.summary: Licence fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
dog_rules.quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

dog_rules.summary: With proof of a current licence and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
dog_rules.quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A licence costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: Licence fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).

dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.

parking_rules.summary: Overnight street parking is banned citywide from 2 AM to 6 AM. Garage and lot permits are the alternative.
parking_rules.quote: Is overnight, on-street parking allowed in White Plains? No. The City has a long-standing ordinance which prohibits parking on the street between the hours of 2:00 AM - 6:00 AM.

parking_rules.summary: Garage and lot permits are sold monthly, quarterly or annually. Resident-only permits need a lease or utility bill, a New York licence with a White Plains address and a vehicle registration with the same information, so an out-of-state licence or registration would not qualify for resident-only locations.
parking_rules.quote: Valid New York drivers license showing resident parker's name and a City of White Plains address Vehicle Registration for each plate number listed on permit with same information as license

parking_rules.summary: The city runs eight garages and 23 surface lots; permits are sold monthly, quarterly or annually and guarantee a space. Monthly prices are on a separate garages-and-lots page that was not read.
parking_rules.quote: Customers may purchase most permits on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis (some restrictions apply) at a considerable discount from the published meter rates.

parking_rules.summary: A $75 annual Resident Evening & Weekend Permit lets residents use most downtown garages Mon-Fri 6 PM-midnight and weekends 10 AM-midnight. No guest street permit was found.
parking_rules.quote: This permit is valid January through December at a cost of $75 and offers White Plains Residents the ability to utilize most downtown parking structures while dining or shopping.

parking_rules.summary: Downtown street meters run Monday to Saturday 9 AM-9 PM (9 AM-6 PM outside downtown); street parking is free on Sundays and six holidays. Meters in lots and garages charge at all times.
parking_rules.quote: On-street meters require payment Monday through Saturday, in the downtown area from 9AM-9PM. On-street meters outside the downtown area require payment 9AM-6PM. On-street parking is free on Sundays

parking_rules.summary: Do not park on the street when it snows or snow is forecast; cars left out may be plowed in and ticketed.
parking_rules.quote: DO NOT PARK CARS ON THE STREET WHEN IT SNOWS - OR WHEN SNOW IS IN THE FORECAST.

dog_rules.summary: Every dog must be licensed. Fee: $10 for one year if spayed or neutered, $18 if not (two-year: $17 / $27).
dog_rules.quote: Spayed/Neutered $10.00 $17.00

dog_rules.summary: Off the owner's property, dogs must be on a leash no longer than eight feet; fine up to $100.
dog_rules.quote: Section 2 - In all other cases, dog owners must have their dogs on leashes not exceeding eight feet in length. Violations are punishable by a fine of up to $100.

dog_rules.summary: Owners must remove their dog's feces from any sidewalk, gutter, street or other public area.
dog_rules.quote: Section 3 - It shall be the duty of each dog owner to remove any feces left by his/her dog on any sidewalk, gutter, street or other public areas.

dog_rules.summary: Two city dog parks, by permit: Bark Park (Main St. extension off Brockway Pl.) and Battle Hill Park. There is an area only for small or young dogs; a current licence tag is required. The Fall/Winter 2025-26 brochure lists the annual fee as $25 for up to 3 dogs per resident, $50 non-resident.
dog_rules.quote: Dogs with permits are welcome to run around and exercise at our Dog Park. This park features an area exclusively for small or young dogs.

safety.geography: NYPD 47th Precinct (Bronx), about 164,000 residents (2020 Census blocks inside the precinct, estimate)

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's licence check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A licence costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.
